ladder.classBlurb: The Cleric serves the hidden faces of their god, carrying blessings that walk unseen through the veil.
The Cleric stands between Heaven and Hell, judging souls and calling down either mercy or punishment.
The Cleric learns the faith of change, calling miracles that refuse to happen the same way twice.
The Cleric hears the sins of the deep, bringing light into darkness that has never seen a prayer.
The Cleric's prayers reach the deep heart of life, healing that remembers every wound and undoes it.
The Cleric preaches across horizons, their faith followed by pilgrims from many worlds.
The Cleric learns faith with nothing to hold onto, a belief so pure it works even where gods cannot hear.
The Cleric gathers prayers that their gods forgot, answering them with power that should no longer exist.
The Cleric touches the faith that came before gods, the first reverence of the world for its own making.

subclasses.ds: Clerics of a god of magic, blending divine and arcane. (Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide)
A cleric who channels starlight rather than a single god's word, pulling gravity and stepping briefly into an incorporeal astral form.
A cleric who channels fire rather than a single domain of a living god, wreathing melee strikes and allies in flame.
Clerics of smithing gods who craft and armor. (Xanathar's Guide to Everything)

Grave Domain expands the fantasy and gameplay style of the Cleric class.
 This subclass focuses on a unique identity, combat role, and spell progression.
A cleric of a death deity who serves as intermediary between the living and the dead, guiding souls both ways.
Clerics of lore, learning, and secrets. (Player's Handbook)
The purest healing-focused cleric — every restoration spell goes further, and the domain's whole identity is keeping a party standing.
Clerics of dawn, fire, and truth who wield radiance as a weapon. (Player's Handbook)
Clerics of wild gods of beasts and growth. (Player's Handbook)
Clerics of law, discipline, and authority. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
Clerics of harmony who bind allies together. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
A cleric who inscribes divine runes onto surfaces and allies, turning the battlefield into a sacred text.
Clerics of storm and sea. (Player's Handbook)
Clerics of mischief and deception. (Player's Handbook)
Clerics who guard the night — protectors against darkness and despair. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
Clerics of battle gods. (Player's Handbook)

ladder.classBlurb: The Druid guards groves hidden in fog, stepping between trees that lead to places no map holds.
The Druid tends the gardens of Heaven and the ashlands of Hell, mastering fire that burns and flowers that heal.
The Druid embraces nature's wildness, changing forms faster and stranger than any law of life allows.
The Druid's roots reach into the abyss, drawing up drowned life and monstrous shapes from the deep.
The Druid becomes one with the living heart of the world, each forest an extension of their body.
The Druid scatters life across horizons, seeding strange worlds and calling beasts from beyond the stars.
The Druid learns that empty ground is also nature, wielding stillness, frost and decay as freely as growth.
The Druid grows forests the world forgets, places that shelter allies and swallow pursuers whole.
The Druid touches the first life of the world and can call its oldest beasts and forests back into being.

subclasses.ds: Druids tied to the fey realm of dreams. (Xanathar's Guide to Everything)
A druid who tends decay the way others tend growth, wielding withering touch and spreading spore clouds.
Druids who embrace decay as part of the natural cycle. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)

Circle of Stars expands the fantasy and gameplay style of the Druid class.
 This subclass focuses on a unique identity, combat role, and spell progression.
Druids of destructive and renewing flame. (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything)
A druid balanced between a light aspect and a dark one, shifting stance to change what their Wild Shape carries.
A druid bonded to a specific terrain, drawing extra spells and resilience from the land itself rather than from an animal bond.
Druids who master Wild Shape for combat. (Player's Handbook)
Druids of ocean and storm, carrying the sea's fury with them. (Player's Handbook (2024))
Druids who speak for the wild and lead summoned animals and fey. (Xanathar's Guide to Everything)
A druid attuned to the raw power of storms — lightning, wind, and the chaos of the tempest.
A druid who has become a prophet of natural law, reading the future in the behaviour of animals and plants.
